an1.150:1.1: Another ten roots of dispute, this time equivalent to [an10.43](). | This chapter deals with technicalities of Vinaya. This emphasis suggests that these portions, and perhaps the Book of the Ones as a whole, was designed as a primer for newly-ordained monastics. If so, it would follow on from the Khuddakapāṭha (“Basic Passages”, Kp 1), which was a textbook for novices. | Generally, for technical Vinaya terms I follow the renderings of Brahmali.
an1.152-159:1.1: These are legal distinctions applying to various classes of Vinaya rules. The most serious offenses are the _parajika_ (“expulsion”) and _saṅghādisesa_ (“suspension”) rules, which are “heavy” and “grave”. All other offenses are “light” and “minor”, since they can largely be cleared with a simple confession, and in some cases the relinquishment of an object such as cloth. This distinction is purely legalistic, however, as some “minor” offenses can be morally serious, for example lying or killing animals. The _parajika_ and _saṅghādisesa_ rules are distinguished in that one who commits _parajika_ is permanently expelled from the Saṅgha with no possibility of rehabilitation, and hence is “incurable” and “not requiring amends”, whereas one who commits a _saṅghādisesa_ is temporarily suspended but reinstated after a period of rehabilitation involving the Saṅgha.
